claude-code.label: Claude Code, interactive session
claude-code.prompt_extra: When a NEXT line tells you to wait, start that command as a background command and end your turn: its exit is what wakes you. Do not run it in the foreground and do not poll its output.
claude-code.coordinator_note: NOTE: Claude Code asks its user before commands; for a room without interruptions the owner starts it with claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
claude-code.status: profile checked by the test suite; worked live rooms on Windows as coordinator and as remote agents on the same PC and on another machine (2026-10-10)

claude-code-headless.label: Claude Code, headless (claude -p)
claude-code-headless.prompt_extra: Run the wait command in the foreground with a command time limit of 10 minutes (timeout 600000). When it says nothing arrived, run it again.
claude-code-headless.coordinator_note: NOTE: Claude Code asks its user before commands; for a room without interruptions the owner starts it with claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
claude-code-headless.status: worked a rehearsal room on Windows on a light and a standard model at low effort, given only the start prompt (2026-10-10)

codex.label: Codex CLI
codex.prompt_extra: The wait command runs for up to 4 minutes. Start it, then keep waiting on that same running command until it exits; do not start a second one. When it says nothing arrived, run it again at once: a wait that ends with nothing is normal, not an error, and it is never a reason to stop. You never stop waiting on your own; only your user, or a message from the room that tells you to, ends it. If the command above is refused or cannot start, change nothing, stop, and tell your user to start you again with codex --yolo.
codex.coordinator_note: NOTE: start Codex with codex --yolo: without it Codex keeps asking its user and its sandbox blocks the room's commands
codex.status: worked live rooms on Windows as remote agents, up to five in one room on one machine (2026-10-12): must be started with codex --yolo; took a wait that timed out (then exit 3, shown by its shell as 1) for a failure and stopped waiting, so a timed-out wait now exits 0 and says it is normal; is never parked (park_after 0), the owner stops it
